history.name: heavy_edge_embedding
history.description: Grow the mapping outward from the single most strongly interacting logical pair, always extending along the heaviest unplaced logical edge whose endpoint touches an already-placed qubit. This greedily packs frequently-interacting logical qubits into adjacent physical qubits.

history.name: activity_centrality_rank_match
history.description: Sort logical qubits by total interaction activity and physical qubits by graph centrality, then assign by matching ranks. The most-talkative logical qubits land on the best-connected physical qubits, minimizing average routing distance to everything else.

history.name: bfs_anchor_growth
history.description: Pick a single anchor pair (most-active logical → most-central physical) and grow the mapping via a priority-queue BFS over the logical interaction graph, placing each newly popped logical qubit on the closest free physical qubit to its already-placed interaction partners. This is a node-priority dual to heavy_edge_embedding.

history.name: bfs_pair_anchor_growth
history.description: BFS-grown placement seeded by the heaviest logical edge placed on adjacent central physical qubits, then identical priority-queue growth as the parent.

This aligns global cluster structure of the program with global cluster structure of the hardware.

def init_mapping(self):
    from collections import defaultdict

    N = self.num_qubits
    dist = self.distance_matrix

    # 1. Build logical interaction weights from self.access (DAG not yet built).
    weight = defaultdict(int)          # weight[(a,b)] with a<b
    logical_degree = defaultdict(int)  # total interaction count per logical
    logical_seen = set()
    for gate_id, qubits in self.access.items():
        if len(qubits) == 2:
            a, b = qubits[0], qubits[1]
            if a == b:
                logical_seen.add(a)
                continue
            u, v = (a, b) if a < b else (b, a)
            weight[(u, v)] += 1
            logical_degree[a] += 1
            logical_degree[b] += 1
            logical_seen.add(a)
            logical_seen.add(b)

    def w(a, b):
        if a == b:
            return 0
        u, v = (a, b) if a < b else (b, a)
        return weight.get((u, v), 0)

    # 2. Initialize outputs as identity; we will overwrite placements.
    self.mapping_dict = list(range(N))
    self.reverse_mapping_dict = list(range(N))

    placed = {}           # logical -> physical
    used_physical = set()

    unplaced_logical = set(q for q in logical_seen if 0 <= q < N)

    def pick_best_physical_for(L):
        best_p = None
        best_cost = None
        for p in range(N):
            if p in used_physical:
                continue
            cost = 0.0
            for P_log, P_phys in placed.items():
                wt = w(L, P_log)
                if wt == 0:
                    continue
                cost += wt * dist[p][P_phys]
            if best_cost is None or cost < best_cost or (cost == best_cost and (best_p is None or p < best_p)):
                best_cost = cost
                best_p = p
        return best_p

    # 3. Seed with the heaviest interacting pair.
    if weight and unplaced_logical:
        (u_seed, v_seed), _ = max(
            weight.items(),
            key=lambda kv: (kv[1], -(kv[0][0] + kv[0][1]))
        )
        if u_seed in unplaced_logical and v_seed in unplaced_logical:
            # Place u_seed at the most central physical (min sum of distances).
            best_p = None
            best_sum = None
            for p in range(N):
                s = sum(dist[p][q] for q in range(N))
                if best_sum is None or s < best_sum or (s == best_sum and p < best_p):
                    best_sum = s
                    best_p = p
            placed[u_seed] = best_p
            used_physical.add(best_p)
            unplaced_logical.discard(u_seed)

            # Place v_seed minimizing w(u,v)*dist.
            p_v = pick_best_physical_for(v_seed)
            if p_v is not None:
                placed[v_seed] = p_v
                used_physical.add(p_v)
                unplaced_logical.discard(v_seed)

    # 4-5. Greedy insertion loop.
    while unplaced_logical:
        best_L = None
        best_score = None
        best_deg = None
        for L in unplaced_logical:
            score = 0
            for P_log in placed:
                score += w(L, P_log)
            deg = logical_degree.get(L, 0)
            if (best_score is None
                or score > best_score
                or (score == best_score and deg > best_deg)
                or (score == best_score and deg == best_deg and (best_L is None or L < best_L))):
                best_score = score
                best_deg = deg
                best_L = L
        if best_L is None:
            break

        if best_score == 0 and not placed:
            # No interactions at all — drop into central placement.
            best_p = None
            best_sum = None
            for p in range(N):
                if p in used_physical:
                    continue
                s = sum(dist[p][q] for q in range(N))
                if best_sum is None or s < best_sum:
                    best_sum = s
                    best_p = p
            p_choice = best_p
        else:
            p_choice = pick_best_physical_for(best_L)

        if p_choice is None:
            break
        placed[best_L] = p_choice
        used_physical.add(p_choice)
        unplaced_logical.discard(best_L)

    # 6. Write placements; fill unused logical slots with remaining physicals.
    assigned_logicals = set(placed.keys())
    free_physicals = [p for p in range(N) if p not in used_physical]
    free_idx = 0
    mapping = [None] * N
    for L in range(N):
        if L in placed:
            mapping[L] = placed[L]
        else:
            # Prefer identity if free, else take next free physical.
            if L not in used_physical and L < N and L not in assigned_logicals:
                # Check identity slot availability.
                pass
            # Use identity if available.
            if L < N and (L not in used_physical):
                mapping[L] = L
                used_physical.add(L)
            else:
                while free_idx < len(free_physicals) and free_physicals[free_idx] in used_physical:
                    free_idx += 1
                if free_idx < len(free_physicals):
                    mapping[L] = free_physicals[free_idx]
                    used_physical.add(free_physicals[free_idx])
                    free_idx += 1
                else:
                    mapping[L] = L  # last-resort fallback

    # Final safety: ensure every slot filled uniquely.
    seen = set()
    remaining = [p for p in range(N) if p not in seen and p not in set(x for x in mapping if x is not None)]
    for i in range(N):
        if mapping[i] is None or mapping[i] in seen:
            # take from remaining
            while remaining and remaining[0] in seen:
                remaining.pop(0)
            mapping[i] = remaining.pop(0) if remaining else i
        seen.add(mapping[i])

    self.mapping_dict = mapping
    self.reverse_mapping_dict = [0] * N
    for L in range(N):
        self.reverse_mapping_dict[mapping[L]] = L

    assert len(set(self.mapping_dict)) == len(self.mapping_dict)

reflections:
INVARIANTS_TO_PRESERVE
- Two-qubit interaction graph weighted by gate frequency drives every decision (top-1 and top-3 build `qig` directly; top-2 implicitly respects it via gate-order traversal). Future gens must keep an interaction-frequency signal as the primary placement currency.
- Hardware coupling structure is consulted via local expansion, not random allocation: top-1 and top-3 grow BFS regions from high-degree seeds; top-2 walks shortest paths along `backend_connections`. Locality on the device graph is load-bearing.
- Bijective full-N mapping with deterministic, seed-stable tie-breakers (fixed `Random(42)`, `min(best)`, sort by `(-degree, id)`). Reproducibility is non-negotiable.

AXES_WITH_ROOM
- Placement objective inside a region: top-1 minimizes weighted shortest-path cost to already-placed partners; top-3 just zips degree-sorted lists; top-2 sidesteps the question. Top-1's lower swap count suggests **partner-aware cost minimization beats positional zipping** — push further with multi-partner weighting (sum of `w * d^2`) rather than linear `w * d`.
- Seeding rule for the next community/region: all three pick the highest-degree free physical node. Top-2's reverse-traversal hints that **seeds informed by gate-order (first interacting community first, not largest first)** may better front-load the early swap-heavy section.
- Use of circuit time / DAG order: top-2 is the only one that consults gate sequence; top-1 and top-3 treat the circuit as a static multigraph. **Adding a recency or early-gate weight to `qig` edges** (heavier weight for gates near t=0) likely helps because early misplacements cascade.

STRUCTURAL_STRENGTHS_AND_GAPS
- Strong on circuits with clear modular community structure on a coupling graph that has dense high-degree clusters (heavy-hex, grid with hubs): community → BFS region is a near-direct embedding, and label propagation converges fast on these.
- Weak on circuits whose interaction graph is near-uniform or expander-like (e.g., QAOA on random graphs, all-to-all-ish kernels): label propagation collapses to one giant community, region growth covers the whole device, and intra-community ordering reduces to degree-sort with no signal — top-3's behavior degenerates here.

UNTESTED_DIRECTIONS
- Spectral / Fiedler-vector partitioning of the QIG to replace label propagation when modularity is low; gives a continuous embedding usable as a tiebreaker even on expanders.
- Iterative refinement pass (Kernighan–Lin-style pairwise swap of placed logical qubits minimizing total `w * d`) after the greedy placement — none of the top-3 do any post-hoc local search.

INVARIANTS_TO_PRESERVE
- Decisions are driven by the circuit's 2-qubit access pattern, not by the identity mapping — every top-3 heuristic reads `self.access` and couples placement to observed interactions.
- BFS / shortest-path distance on the physical coupling graph is the universal spatial primitive; all three evaluate candidate placements through graph distance rather than coordinate geometry.
- Each produces a strictly bijective permutation via deterministic backfill of unused physical qubits — no stochastic fallbacks, no duplicate physical IDs.

AXES_WITH_ROOM
- Cost-function curvature for within-region placement: top-1 uses Σ w·d (linear), top-2 uses Σ w·d² (quadratic), top-3 uses implicit swap-cost from simulation. Top-1 beats top-2 (638.8 vs 641.6). Hypothesis: linear is better because quadratic over-penalizes unavoidable long edges between hub qubits and collapses candidate sets into local minima; a sub-quadratic shape (e.g., d^1.3 or log(1+d)) is the direction to probe.
- Seeding rule: top-1/top-2 seed each region at the maximum-degree available physical qubit and anchor the highest intra-weight logical to it; top-3 seeds at the identity and learns via simulation — and it is clearly worst (675.9). Hypothesis: degree-aware anchoring is load-bearing; further gains should come from anchoring by centrality/eccentricity, not from dropping it.
- Global strategy: community-partition-then-place (top-1/2) dominates trajectory-learned placement (top-3) by ~37 swaps. Hypothesis: explicit partitioning beats implicit routing-learned placement because it constrains search before commitments are made.

STRUCTURAL_STRENGTHS_AND_GAPS
- Strong on modular / block-structured circuits (repeated localized 2q subblocks, QAOA-style layers): label-propagation finds the blocks and BFS-region growing isolates them on the device so inter-block traffic stays low.
- Weak on circuits with near-uniform or long-range sparse interaction graphs — label propagation collapses everything into one giant community (or spurious ones), and both top-1/2 place communities independently, never optimizing *inter*-community boundaries; top-2's squared cost makes this worse by amplifying unavoidable long hops.

UNTESTED_DIRECTIONS
- Temporal/DAG-depth weighting of interactions: none of the top-3 weight early or critical-path gates more than late ones — the QIG is a flat multiset. Try a linear or exponential gate-index decay so the initial placement privileges the first layers (where swaps cost the most downstream).
- Inter-community boundary alignment: no top-3 heuristic places communities with awareness of cross-community QIG edges. Introduce a primitive that orders communities by cross-edge weight and snaps each community's seed to a physical node adjacent to the previous community's boundary.

INVARIANTS_TO_PRESERVE
- Label-propagation community detection on the weighted qubit-interaction graph (20 iterations, deterministic seed=42, min-label tie-break) — all three rely on this to define placement regions.
- Largest-community-first, BFS-grown physical region seeded by max-degree available node, with degree-tiered frontier expansion. This guarantees each community occupies a topologically dense contiguous patch.
- Within a region, placement is anchor-then-greedy: highest intra-community weight logical qubit is pinned to the highest-degree physical node, then remaining qubits are inserted one at a time minimizing a Σ w·f(d) cost against already-placed partners.

AXES_WITH_ROOM
- Distance-penalty shape: top-1 uses f(d)=d (linear), top-2 f(d)=d² (super-linear), top-3 f(d)=log(1+d) (sub-linear). Linear wins by ~3–5 swaps. Hypothesis: on shallow communities whose diameter ≤ 2–3, squaring overweights marginal 1-vs-2 differences and log flattens them. A piecewise cost (linear up to region diameter, then saturating) is likely the correct middle ground.
- Anchor choice: all three pick the single highest-intra-weight logical on the single highest-degree physical. Hypothesis: anchoring on a 2-node *edge* (the heaviest intra-community interaction) onto the heaviest physical edge should reduce first-swap pressure, since the dominant gate is already adjacent.
- Partner set for greedy scoring: all use only *already-placed* partners. Hypothesis: including *unplaced* partners with a discounted weight (lookahead-1) would stop the first few placements from being made in near-blind conditions.

STRUCTURAL_STRENGTHS_AND_GAPS
- Strong on circuits with clear modular / block-diagonal interaction structure (e.g., QAOA on clustered graphs, layered VQE ansätze) because label-propagation cleanly separates blocks and BFS regions map them to dense patches.
- Weak on circuits with a single giant near-clique or uniform all-to-all interaction (e.g., full QFT, dense Hamiltonian sims): label propagation collapses everything into one community larger than any dense physical region, so BFS overflows into sparse territory and the greedy placement degrades to arbitrary order.

UNTESTED_DIRECTIONS
- Time-weighted interaction graph: weight each 2-qubit gate by 1/(1+gate_index) or by a decaying window, so early-circuit interactions dominate placement — none of the three uses gate order, only counts.
- Multi-start / community-pair co-placement: jointly place the two largest communities using inter-community edge weights to choose *which* dense regions they occupy, instead of the current purely greedy largest-first region grabbing.
